feedback.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:   

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[{e}^{x+y}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{1+y}-{e}^{0+y})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{1+y}-{e}^{y})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(e{e}^{y}-{e}^{y})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{y}(e-1)\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{y}(e-1)\text{d}y & =(e-1)[{e}^{y}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =(e-1)({e}^{2}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =(e-1)({e}^{2}-1) \\  & ={e}^{3}-{e}^{2}-e+1\end{aligned}
$$
